key_highlights: ASX finished flat; miners rose while oil stocks struggled and IDP plummeted, with tech leading a Wall Street-driven rally
RBA set to hike again as inflation tests the bank's credibility; household spending under pressure
Australian flash PMI sags, signalling softening domestic demand
Gold miners active: Critical Resources surges on Suriname grab, Aurum raises $52.5M, Meridian +10% on Cabaçal $2bn study, Platina secures Rio cheque
Fuel price fears mount as global buffers dry up; Aramco eyes Yanbu restart; oil falls on Iran Hormuz reopening report
Property market weakens: rising listings, falling demand pushing prices lower
Jetstar industrial action escalates with staff waiving baggage/seat fees
World economy growing wary of US; Trump-Xi AI divide keeps investors hedged
Nuclear energy debate intensifies in Australia; data centres strain net-zero targets
Syngenis gains precision medicine firepower; healthcare innovation continues

sectors.trend: Miners outperformed on the day; gold names particularly active with multiple catalysts (Critical Resources, Aurum, Meridian, Platina). Rare earths (Critica/Jupiter) gaining offtake traction. Oil-related miners under pressure.
sectors.implications: Gold rotation continues as safe-haven demand rises amid US-China tensions and RBA hikes. Rare earths offer structural upside. Oil miners face headwinds from Aramco restart and Iran Hormuz signals.

sectors.trend: Oil stocks struggled as global supply signals (Aramco Yanbu restart, Iran Hormuz offer) pressured prices. Fuel cost fears for Australia as buffers dry up. Nuclear energy debate and data-centre power demand add policy uncertainty.
sectors.implications: Short-term oil price volatility hurts Woodside (WDS.AX) and Santos (STO.AX). Nuclear debate could benefit uranium names (NexGen, Orano-linked). Fuel cost pass-through pressures consumer margins.

sectors.trend: Tech led ASX higher on Wall Street spillover. AI theme dominant globally; $16b Aussie tech firm faces China-link controversy. AI self-regulation warnings mount.
sectors.implications: ASX tech (CSL.AX biotech-adjacent, Syngenis) benefits from innovation flows. China-linked exposure creates geopolitical risk. AI capex cycle supports data-centre REITs but strains net-zero credentials.

sectors.trend: RBA rate hikes squeeze household spending, pressuring NPL trajectories. PMI softness signals weaker credit demand. Debt cliff concerns for federal/state governments.
sectors.implications: Big Four banks (CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX) benefit from higher NIM but face rising credit costs. Government debt trajectory pressures sovereign bond yields.

sectors.trend: Jetstar industrial action escalates; airlines cutting capacity on $1B Q4 fuel surge. Household spending squeezed by RBA hikes. Property demand falling.
sectors.implications: Qantas (QAN.AX) and Jetstar face margin pressure from fuel and industrial action. Consumer discretionary (WES.AX, WBC.AX retail) under pressure. REITs (GPG.AX, SPG.AX) face falling demand.

sectors.trend: Syngenis gains precision medicine venture; global biotech active (Ultragenyx FDA approval, Twist Bioscience AI drug discovery).
sectors.implications: CSL.AX and Syngenis (SYG.AX) benefit from innovation pipeline. AI-driven drug discovery accelerates R&D timelines.

Gold and rare earths rotation as safe-haven/strategic demand rises
Oil supply recovery (Aramco, Iran) pressuring energy equities
AI geopolitical divide (US-China) driving tech bifurcation
Australian property market cooling: listings up, demand down
Fuel cost transmission to consumer and transport sectors
Nuclear energy policy debate and data-centre power demand
PMI softening signals domestic demand weakness

risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor RBA statements; favour rate-sensitive financials with strong NIM; hedge with inflation-linked bonds

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Fuel price spike and global buffer depletion
risk_assessment.mitigation: Underweight oil-exposed transport (QAN.AX); favour domestic energy producers with hedged contracts

risk_assessment.risk_factor: US-China geopolitical and AI trade divide
risk_assessment.mitigation: Diversify away from China-revenue-dependent ASX tech; monitor Trump-Xi outcomes
Reduce consumer discretionary exposure; favour defensive staples (WES.AX, WOL.AX)
Avoid QAN.AX near-term; monitor Jetstar wage settlement

risk_assessment.risk_factor: El Nino and climate-related commodity risk
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor agricultural and insurance exposures; favour diversified miners

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold miners and rare earths on safe-haven and strategic demand
opportunities.rationale: Multiple catalysts: Critical Resources Suriname grab, Aurum $52.5M raise, Meridian $2bn Cabaçal study, Platina Rio cheque; Critica/Jupiter rare earth offtake

opportunities.recommendation: Selective tech exposure via ASX-listed AI/biotech innovators
opportunities.rationale: Tech led ASX higher; Syngenis precision medicine and global AI drug discovery partnerships support sector

opportunities.recommendation: Tactical long on Big Four banks on RBA hike cycle
opportunities.rationale: Higher rates support NIM; credit costs manageable if PMI stabilises

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce exposure to oil-exposed transport and energy names
defensive_moves.rationale: Aramco restart, Iran Hormuz signals, and $1B Q4 fuel surge pressure margins; Jetstar industrial action adds risk

defensive_moves.recommendation: Underweight property REITs and consumer discretionary
defensive_moves.rationale: Rising listings, falling demand, RBA-squeezed spending, and PMI softening create headwinds

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge AUD/USD and commodity-linked revenue with diversification
defensive_moves.rationale: Global wariness of US, Trump-Xi tensions, and fuel volatility create FX and commodity risk

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely range-bound with sector rotation: miners/gold and tech outperforming, oil and consumer lagging. RBA hike and PMI softness cap upside. Fuel volatility adds noise. Expect 1-2% range on ^AXJO.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautiously constructive if RBA stabilises and PMI recovers. Gold and rare earths offer structural tailwinds. Property correction may deepen. AI/tech innovation supports select names. Nuclear policy shift could create new energy investment themes.
